classes.name: Penicillins
classes.description: Oral penicillins: amoxicillin (capsules, tablets, chewables, suspension), amoxicillin-clavulanate (Augmentin, Augmentin XR, suspension), penicillin V potassium, dicloxacillin. Amoxicillin-clavulanate belongs to this class.
classes.plainDescription: The most common antibiotic family, for ear, sinus, throat, dental and skin infections.
classes.indication: Ear, sinus, strep throat, dental, skin infections

classes.name: Oral cephalosporins
classes.description: Oral cephalosporins: cephalexin (Keflex), cefadroxil, cefuroxime axetil (Ceftin), cefprozil, cefaclor, cefdinir, cefpodoxime, cefixime (Suprax).
classes.plainDescription: A common antibiotic family for skin, urinary and ear infections, often used with a mild penicillin allergy.
classes.indication: Skin, urinary tract, ear and respiratory infections

classes.name: Macrolides
classes.description: Oral macrolides: azithromycin (Zithromax, Z-Pak, suspension), clarithromycin (Biaxin, ER), erythromycin base/stearate/ethylsuccinate (Ery-Tab, Erythrocin, E.E.S., PCE).
classes.plainDescription: A short-course antibiotic for chest infections and for people allergic to penicillin.

classes.name: Tetracyclines
classes.description: Oral tetracyclines: doxycycline hyclate and monohydrate (Vibramycin, Doryx, Doryx MPC, Acticlate, Targadox; Lymepak discontinued 2025), minocycline IR and ER (Minocin, Solodyn, Minolira, Ximino), tetracycline, sarecycline (Seysara), omadacycline (Nuzyra). Branded doxycycline/minocycline ER products are usually PA or excluded.
classes.plainDescription: Antibiotics for tick bites and Lyme disease, chest infections, MRSA skin infections and acne.
classes.indication: Lyme disease, respiratory and skin infections, acne

classes.name: Fluoroquinolones
classes.description: Oral fluoroquinolones: ciprofloxacin (Cipro), levofloxacin (Levaquin), moxifloxacin (Avelox), ofloxacin, delafloxacin (Baxdela). Not ophthalmic/otic drops.
classes.plainDescription: Strong antibiotics kept for specific infections because of tendon and nerve side effects.
classes.indication: Complicated UTI, pneumonia, specific resistant infections

classes.name: Urinary tract antibiotics
classes.description: Agents used mainly for uncomplicated urinary tract infection: nitrofurantoin (Macrobid, Macrodantin, suspension), sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (Bactrim, Bactrim DS), trimethoprim, fosfomycin (Monurol), methenamine hippurate (Hiprex; prophylaxis), and the newer brands pivmecillinam (Pivya), sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid (Orlynvah), gepotidacin (Blujepa; also labeled for gonorrhea since 2025-12). Fluoroquinolones and cephalosporins belong to their own classes.

classes.name: C. difficile treatments
classes.description: Oral treatments for Clostridioides difficile infection: vancomycin capsules and oral solution (Vancocin, Firvanq kit), fidaxomicin (Dificid; an AB-rated generic is approved), fecal microbiota spores (Vowst, recurrence prevention). Metronidazole is an alternative only (guidelines reserve it for non-severe cases when the others are unavailable), never the pick. Rebyota and bezlotoxumab are provider-administered.
classes.plainDescription: Medicines for a serious gut infection that can follow antibiotic use.
